degeneracy_diagnostic.note: eps_hat ~ 0.87-0.9 across Pantheon+/Union3/DESY5 is the near-degeneracy direction: the TEP point that best impersonates flat-LCDM. Any LCDM-consistent catalog returns this amplitude trivially; the discriminating information is in delta_chi2/BF, not the amplitude.

interpretation: Independent-catalog consistency check. DES-SN5YR prefers the TEP direction at delta_chi2 = -0.61 (covtot) / -1.54 (diag-only), with epsilon_MLE = 0.892 -- numerically consistent with Pantheon+ (0.874) and Union3 (0.856). The preference is weaker than Pantheon+'s -3.8 because DES-SN5YR (a) contains no Cepheid-anchor calibrator block, (b) is already an excellent LCDM fit (chi2/dof 0.898), and (c) is dominated by high-z objects where both frames converge. The localization mirrors Pantheon+: gains in the low-z/intermediate blocks, a small loss at z>0.7. Caveat: the epsilon~0.87-0.9 cross-catalog stability is a degeneracy-direction rediscovery (rms distance-modulus difference vs LCDM is ~0.02 mag, an order below typical MUERR), so it does NOT constitute independent replication -- only delta_chi2/BF discriminates, and those are small here. Verdict: direction replicates; significance does not, consistent with a calibrator-free catalog having little power over the near-degenerate direction.
